verdict_summary: Substantive workflow-hygiene drift surfaced. The L19 lens caught the #1333-mini-rev-named gap (phase-2a-exit-criteria.yml MISSING the §3.5o env vars despite the mini-rev BELONGS-NAMED-NOW disposition) AS STILL OPEN at base SHA 4bbc4cac, plus a much wider §3.5o-coverage gap (only 3 of ~24 Rust-compiling workflows have the full env vars), plus a substantive branch-protection.yml-spec ↔ live drift (spec lists 28 contexts; live only enforces 11; live also enforces 1 context — API drift detector — not in the spec), plus action-pin drift (admin-shell-e2e.yml uses tag-pinned actions vs the workspace SHA-pinned norm), plus one RETIRED no-op job hanging on (wasm-browser.yml::cross-browser-determinism-retired). No BLOCKERs (none of the drift breaks shippable CI today); 2 MAJOR (§3.5o coverage + branch-protection drift); 4 MINOR (RETIRED job, admin-shell-e2e pin drift, vitest sibling-file drift, msrv.yml env-var gap inside a workflow that explicitly documents disk-pressure in its own comments); 1 OBS.
disposition: ITERATE — R6 R1 surfaced MAJOR-class findings; orchestrator triage required; per Q5 cadence + iterate-to-convergence (CLAUDE.md §9 + feedback_iterate_critical_reviews_to_convergence) re-fire full L1-Lx council on edited artifact after R6-FP closes findings. NOT yet R6-convergence.
r6_r1_convergence_disposition: NOT-CONVERGED — 2 MAJOR + 4 MINOR + 1 OBS surfaced; expect at least one R6-FP cycle then R6 R2 full council.

findings.title: §3.5o disk-OOM env vars MISSING from ~21 of ~24 Rust-compiling workflows (only ci.yml + coverage.yml + wasm-conformance.yml have them); the named #1333-mini-rev origin (phase-2a-exit-criteria.yml) is STILL OPEN at base SHA 4bbc4cac despite the BELONGS-NAMED-NOW disposition
findings.evidence: Audit of all 34 workflow files at SHA 4bbc4cac: workflows that install a Rust toolchain via dtolnay/rust-toolchain@ OR run any `cargo {build,check,test,clippy,nextest,doc,bench,tree,deny,audit,vet,mutants,public-api}` invocation = ~30. Of those, only 3 carry both `CARGO_INCREMENTAL: 0` AND `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG: line-tables-only` in their `env:` block: ci.yml (lines 76-77), coverage.yml (lines 44+, see env block at L43), wasm-conformance.yml (env block at L48). The §3.5o codification (added 2026-05-22, dispatch-conventions.md L1571) is explicit: 'Apply at workflow-env scope so every matrix leg inherits' on every Rust-compile-doing workflow. Workflows missing them include: phase-2a-exit-criteria.yml (the explicitly-named #1333 mini-rev origin: env block at L38 has only CARGO_TERM_COLOR + RUST_BACKTRACE + BENTEN_BENCH_GATE_MULTIPLIER), msrv.yml (no env block; comments at L71-73 explicitly document disk-pressure that triggered fixture-test scope-narrowing — the workflow knows about disk-OOM yet doesn't apply the §3.5o fix), multi-arch-cargo-check.yml (no top-level env block; only free-disk-space step), bundle-size.yml, determinism.yml, fuzz.yml, host-error-wire-safety.yml, cross-process-graph.yml, cross-browser-determinism.yml, supply-chain.yml, wasm-browser.yml, wasm-checks.yml, wasm-runtime.yml, cite-drift.yml, codeql.yml, admin-shell-e2e.yml, bench.yml, cargo-public-api.yml, cargo-vet.yml, mutants.yml, supply-chain-seeded-test.yml, napi-vitest.yml, packages-engine-vitest.yml, devserver-vitest.yml. The #1333 mini-rev (.addl/phase-4-meta/r5-g-core-10-pr-b-mini-review.json line 68) disposed this as `BELONGS-NAMED-NOW = follow-up ci(phase-2a-exit): add CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 + Free disk space step per §3.5o`. Per HARD RULE 12 clause (b) BELONGS-NAMED-NOW requires the destination to receive the entry NOW; the destination (a follow-up commit/PR/issue) does not appear to have landed (no commits touch phase-2a-exit-criteria.yml env block between the mini-rev date and base SHA 4bbc4cac, and the issue search surfaces nothing matching `ci(phase-2a-exit): CARGO_INCREMENTAL`).
findings.ground_truth_verify: Grep verification at base SHA 4bbc4cac: `grep -l CARGO_INCREMENTAL .github/workflows/*.yml` returns exactly ci.yml, coverage.yml, wasm-conformance.yml — 3 of ~30 Rust-compiling workflows. `grep -n CARGO_INCREMENTAL .github/workflows/phase-2a-exit-criteria.yml` returns 0 matches. The §3.5o codification at .addl/dispatch-conventions.md L1571-1585 is explicit on the rule.
findings.disposition: FIX-NOW — single R6-FP commit applies §3.5o env vars (the 2 env vars + a `Free disk space` step where missing) to every Rust-compile-doing workflow. Atomic-shape: add a top-level `env:` block with `CARGO_INCREMENTAL: 0` + `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG: line-tables-only` to each workflow currently lacking it, and add the `- uses: ./.github/actions/free-disk-space` step (with `if: runner.os == 'Linux'`) immediately after checkout on every Linux job leg. Per §3.5o the macOS legs are no-ops there. This closes the #1333 mini-rev BELONGS-NAMED-NOW gap (which was the explicit catalog-driver for this L19 question) plus generalizes the fix to the full workflow fleet (the deeper pattern §3.5o codifies).

findings.title: Branch-protection LIVE state diverges from .github/branch-protection.yml spec (spec = 28 required contexts, live = 11; live also enforces 1 context that is NOT in the spec)
findings.evidence: Diff at SHA 4bbc4cac: live required_status_checks.contexts returns 11 entries: ['cross-leg byte-equality gate (T9)', 'create-benten-app cold install', 'release-build (--no-default-features) gate', 'T9 cross-leg byte-equality gate', 'Phase 2a exit-gate aggregate', 'docs ↔ Rust enum ↔ TS types parity', 'self-test (meta-assertion that the detector actually detects)', 'cargo-deny (licenses / bans / advisories / sources)', 'cargo-audit (belt-and-suspenders)', 'Cargo.lock integrity', 'API drift detector (required-failing per G-CORE-9 FREEZE)']. Spec at .github/branch-protection.yml L177-222 declares 28 entries (the 10 Phase-2a-era frozen + 18 Phase-2b/3 additions: bundle-size 1 + cross-process-graph 1 + cross-browser-determinism 4 + wasm-conformance 1 + wasm-browser 1 + wasm-checks 2 + wasm-runtime 3 + multi-arch-cargo-check 5). Drift is documented as intentional-not-applied at L102-110 ('Phase-2b/3 additions ... became load-bearing during Phase 2b ... but were never promoted to required-status') with an apply-runbook at L13-36 (one-shot PAT-with-admin-scope `gh api PUT`) — but the drift HAS been actively widened post-spec-write by Phase-4-Meta-Core: the G-CORE-9 FREEZE landed 'API drift detector (required-failing per G-CORE-9 FREEZE)' in branch protection live (cargo-public-api.yml job name at line 36; G-CORE-9 R1 triage Fork 3 ratification per workflow header L12-18) yet did NOT update the .github/branch-protection.yml spec to record it. The spec is now drifted on BOTH sides: 17 declared-but-not-applied (Phase-2b/3 carry) + 1 applied-but-not-declared (G-CORE-9 freeze gate). The drift-detector workflow (branch-protection-spec-check.yml) is in warn-only mode (STRICT_PROTECTION_CHECK_DEFAULT: false) so the gap doesn't bite at CI time.
findings.ground_truth_verify: Set-diff at HEAD: `gh api repos/BentenAI/benten-engine/branches/main/protection --jq .required_status_checks.contexts[]` returns 11 entries; `grep -E '^\s+- "' .github/branch-protection.yml | sed 's/.*- "//;s/"//' | sort -u` returns 28 entries. Python set-diff: declared-but-not-applied = 17, applied-but-not-declared = 1 ('API drift detector (required-failing per G-CORE-9 FREEZE)').
findings.disposition: FIX-NOW — two coupled edits: (a) update .github/branch-protection.yml spec to add the `API drift detector (required-failing per G-CORE-9 FREEZE)` context to the required-status-checks list with a brief Phase-4-Meta-Core-G-CORE-9-FREEZE provenance comment; (b) the wider 17-entry declared-but-not-applied gap is a Ben-decision Phase-2a CI-1 follow-up gate (per the spec's own L102-110 narrative — it 'awaits Ben running the apply runbook'). The narrower FIX-NOW (closing the spec's own back-drift from G-CORE-9 freeze) MUST land now. The wider apply-runbook gap = BELONGS-NAMED-NOW in `docs/future/phase-4-backlog.md` as the deferral target (Ben-decision, requires PAT + admin scope) — verify a row already exists; if not, add the explicit row at R6-FP time. Per §3.5g cross-tool config mirror (extended 2026-05-13) + §3.6h-strengthening: when the catalog drifts, the SAME PR/wave landing the fix MUST close the origin instance(s); here this means landing the G-CORE-9 freeze must have updated the spec at G-CORE-9 freeze time (it didn't — that's the §3.6h gap, but per `forward-fire-only-when-origin-already-closed` parenthetical we close-on-discovery-now).

findings.title: wasm-browser.yml::cross-browser-determinism-retired is a RETIRED no-op job still in the workflow file
findings.evidence: The `cross-browser-determinism-retired` job exists only to emit `::warning::This legacy cross-browser-determinism job is RETIRED.`. Per its own L383-385 inline rationale: 'it remains as a no-op only to avoid workflow-id churn at the branch-protection layer.' But it is NOT in branch protection (live or spec) — search for `cross-browser determinism` in either set returns the active per-PR Playwright contexts (chromium/firefox/webkit) at .github/workflows/cross-browser-determinism.yml, not this no-op. The 'workflow-id churn at branch-protection layer' rationale is therefore inactive — the job has no branch-protection-anchor justification.
findings.ground_truth_verify: Confirmed: `gh api repos/BentenAI/benten-engine/branches/main/protection --jq .required_status_checks.contexts[]` does NOT include the retired job name; `grep -n 'cross-browser determinism' .github/branch-protection.yml` returns the 3 active browser contexts.
findings.disposition: FIX-NOW orchestrator-direct — delete the `cross-browser-determinism-retired` job from .github/workflows/wasm-browser.yml (L372-390). 19 LOC removed. Codification note: if any future workflow-id-churn-avoidance rationale resurfaces, restore via git-history pull rather than maintain dead code.

findings.title: admin-shell-e2e.yml uses tag-pinned actions (actions/checkout@v4, dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable, actions/cache@v4) + `macos-latest` + `ubuntu-latest` — drifts from the workspace SHA-pinned + version-pinned norm
findings.evidence: Every other workflow uses SHA-pinned actions (`actions/checkout@93cb6efe...`, `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@29eef336d9b...`, `Swatinem/rust-cache@e18b497...`, `actions/setup-node@49933ea5...`, `taiki-e/install-action@e1c4cd42...`) AND uses pinned runner versions (ubuntu-24.04 / macos-14 / macos-15-intel). admin-shell-e2e.yml uniquely uses tag-pinned + latest. Per supply-chain hygiene + Dependabot rotation per CLAUDE.md commit-conventions implicit norm + the dtolnay/rust-toolchain comment 'no semver tags; Dependabot rotates frequently' (visible in 6+ other workflows), SHA-pinning is the project norm. The tag-pin form lets upstream tags float silently across runs.
findings.ground_truth_verify: Grep verification: `grep -rn 'actions/checkout@v4\|dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable' .github/workflows/*.yml` returns matches only in admin-shell-e2e.yml; `grep -rn 'macos-latest\|ubuntu-latest' .github/workflows/*.yml` (excluding comments/docstrings) shows admin-shell-e2e is the only workflow using `-latest`.
findings.disposition: FIX-NOW orchestrator-direct — bump admin-shell-e2e.yml to SHA-pinned actions (match the ci.yml SHAs) + pin to `macos-14` + `ubuntu-24.04` (the workspace norm). Dependabot already rotates the SHAs. ~6 line-edits.

findings.title: napi-vitest.yml is structurally drifted from sibling packages-engine-vitest.yml — packages-engine-vitest has `Free disk space (composite)` step (L44-47), napi-vitest does not, despite both running the same `cargo + napi-rs build` workload on the same `ubuntu-24.04` runner
findings.evidence: Both workflows: (a) build the napi cdylib via `npm run build` (lines 84-95 + 64-72 respectively); (b) run vitest against the built cdylib; (c) target ubuntu-24.04 with 20-25 minute timeouts. packages-engine-vitest.yml carries a `Free disk space (composite)` step at L44-47 with rationale 'Heavy cargo + napi-rs build; pre-emptively free disk space per the wave-8b disk-pressure carry-forward'. napi-vitest.yml runs the SAME workload (lighter — no top-level npm install + workspace tsc build) without this step. The L19 question 'No workflow-file drift between sibling workflows' explicitly cites these two sibling files as the recurring drift case.
findings.ground_truth_verify: Grep verification: `grep -nE 'Free disk|free-disk' .github/workflows/napi-vitest.yml .github/workflows/packages-engine-vitest.yml` returns 2 matches in packages-engine-vitest.yml (L44+L47), 0 in napi-vitest.yml.
findings.disposition: FIX-NOW orchestrator-direct — add the `Free disk space (composite)` step to napi-vitest.yml immediately after checkout (matching the packages-engine-vitest.yml L44-47 shape) AND add the §3.5o env vars (CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 + CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=line-tables-only) to its env block at L35-37. ~5 LOC. Couples naturally with l19-r1-MAJ-1's wider §3.5o sweep — fold into the same R6-FP commit.

findings.title: msrv.yml does not carry §3.5o env vars despite its own in-source comments at L71-73 documenting the exact disk-OOM-pressure failure mode §3.5o was codified to fix
findings.evidence: msrv.yml L70-77 explicitly documents: 'Wave-8e disk-pressure investigation: under MSRV 1.95 the workspace-wide test build links 100+ binaries each statically pulling wasmtime + cranelift, blowing the GH Actions runner's 14GB disk and producing `ld: SIGBUS` / `No space left on device` failures during the link step. Building only the one test binary that contains the fixture check eliminates 95% of the linker work without losing coverage.' This is EXACTLY the §3.5o failure-mode signature. The workflow's chosen mitigation (scoping the test invocation to a single binary) is a narrower fix than the codified §3.5o discipline (which combines env-var fixes + Free-disk-space step + scoping where applicable). Without the §3.5o env vars, any future cargo addition to the MSRV build can recur disk-OOM. The L71-73 comment is a load-bearing flag that the workflow knows about the pressure mode.
findings.ground_truth_verify: msrv.yml env block at L38-50 has only `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` step; no top-level `env:` block. `grep -n CARGO_INCREMENTAL .github/workflows/msrv.yml` returns 0 matches. The §3.5o codification (dispatch-conventions.md L1571-1585) explicitly identifies disk-OOM/SIGBUS as the same root-cause class.
findings.disposition: FIX-NOW — fold into the l19-r1-MAJ-1 wider §3.5o sweep: add a top-level `env:` block carrying CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 + CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=line-tables-only AND a `Free disk space` step (Linux-only) before the build step. Couples naturally.

findings.title: Clippy MSRV pin (1.95.0) gate is exercised in CI only on the `stable` matrix leg; MSRV legs build+test but do not run clippy
findings.evidence: ci.yml L133-141 explicitly gates fmt + clippy on `matrix.rust == 'stable'` with the rationale comment 'fmt + clippy only on stable to avoid MSRV-chasing lint churn; the MSRV legs still build+test to catch accidental post-1.95 features'. msrv.yml runs `cargo build` and a targeted `cargo test` but no clippy. Per §3.5j codification (dispatch-conventions.md L378+), §3.5j is about the LOCAL pre-push gate needing BOTH MSRV + stable clippy (because 'stable Rust ships clippy lints that MSRV 1.95 lacks; these fire silently in CI but pass locally on MSRV-only checks'). The CI-side single-channel-clippy posture is the inverse asymmetry: CI catches lints stable has, but never exercises MSRV clippy. The L19 question explicitly asks 'Clippy MSRV pin (1.95.0) + stable both wired across workflows + locally per §3.5j (incl. `--features benten-eval/testing,benten-engine/test-helpers,benten-graph/testing` per R3 amendment)?'
findings.ground_truth_verify: ci.yml L141 confirms `--features benten-eval/testing,benten-engine/test-helpers,benten-graph/testing` is wired (R3 amendment satisfied). The single-channel posture is intentional per the in-source rationale comment; the §3.5j framing makes LOCAL discipline carry the MSRV side. OBSERVATION-level (not MINOR): the CI posture is intentional + documented, but the L19 lens flags it as a watch-item because §3.5j's full-defense shape mixes CI single-channel + local-both. If a future commit drifts the MSRV-vs-stable lint surface AND the orchestrator skips local §3.5j pre-push, both gates miss.
findings.disposition: OBSERVE — no action at R6 R1; flagging for the R6-final 'is the CI fleet fully exercising both clippy channels?' question. If §3.5j shows a 2nd recurrence pattern across phases (currently 1-instance at G-CORE-9 R3 L12-R3-MIN-2 per the dispatch-conventions L380 ratification), consider adding an MSRV clippy step gated narrower than the full MSRV build matrix (e.g., a single ubuntu-24.04 MSRV-clippy job, ~5 min added CI time, surfaces MSRV-only lint regressions without enforcing them PR-blocking).

lens_reflection.what_the_lens_is_uniquely_positioned_to_: Process-side hygiene drift in workflow files + the spec ↔ live branch-protection diff (which no other R6 lens surfaces — code-side lenses look at code, threat-model lenses look at adversary frames, doc-coupling lenses look at prose). The §3.5o env-var coverage gap + spec ↔ live drift are pure infrastructure-class surfaces that no other lens has angle on.
lens_reflection.what_this_lens_did_not_check: Per-workflow CORRECTNESS of the cargo invocations themselves (whether the right tests run with the right features) — those are L13 test-coverage lens territory. Per-workflow security posture of dependencies (the cargo-deny rules themselves) — those are L20 supply-chain lens territory if it exists.
lens_reflection.cross_check_pair_notes: This lens has no formal cross-check pair in the R6-LENS-CATALOG.md §'Cross-check pairs' table. Its outputs feed into the §3.6j sweep-completeness-self-verify discipline by exercising the published catalog against live state — a meta-check the catalog itself recommends.
